description: Galbi Korean BBQ Short Ribs are a quintessential Korean dish featuring tender, marinated beef short ribs grilled to perfection. The sweet and savory marinade, often enhanced with Asian pear, soy sauce, garlic, and ginger, infuses the meat with incredible flavor. This beloved dish offers a delightful balance of smoky char and juicy richness, making it a centerpiece for any Korean feast.

ingredients.notes: flanken cut, rinsed and patted dry
peeled and grated (or 1/4 cup apple juice)

instructions.title: Prepare the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse the flanken-cut beef short ribs under cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat them completely dry with paper towels. If the ribs are very thick, you can gently score them a few times across the grain to help them absorb the marinade more effectively. Place the prepared ribs in a large shallow dish or a resealable bag.

instructions.title: Make the Marinade
instructions.text: In a blender or food processor, combine the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, grated Asian pear, and half of the chopped green onions. Blend until the mixture is smooth. If the marinade is too thick, add 2 tablespoons of water to reach a pourable consistency.

instructions.title: Marinate the Ribs
instructions.text: Pour the prepared marinade over the short ribs, ensuring all pieces are thoroughly coated. Massage the marinade into the meat. Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (up to 24 hours), to allow the flavors to fully penetrate the meat.

instructions.title: Preheat Grill
instructions.text: When ready to cook, remove the ribs from the refrigerator 30 minutes before grilling to bring them closer to room temperature. Preheat your outdoor grill to medium-high heat (about 400-450°F / 200-230°C) or preheat your broiler to high. Lightly oil the grill grates or broiler pan to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Short Ribs
instructions.text: Place the marinated short ribs on the hot grill. Cook for 3-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness, flipping occasionally to achieve a nice char and even cooking. For broiler, place ribs on a lined baking sheet and broil 4-6 inches from the heat source for 3-4 minutes per side. Cook until caramelized and cooked through.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, transfer the Galbi to a clean cutting board or serving platter. Let the ribs rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow the juices to redistribute. Garnish with the remaining fresh chopped green onions and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Serve immediately with rice and various banchan (side dishes).

tips: For the most tender ribs, ensure you use flanken-cut short ribs, which are cut across the bone. Marinating overnight allows the enzymes in the Asian pear to tenderize the meat beautifully.
Achieving a good char is key for authentic Galbi flavor. Dont overcrowd your grill to maintain high heat and get those delicious caramelized edges.
Galbi is best served hot off the grill with a bowl of steamed rice and an assortment of banchan like kimchi, pickled radishes, and seasoned spinach.
article:
There are few culinary experiences as universally beloved as Korean BBQ. The sizzling sound, smoky aroma, and communal joy of cooking at the table make it an unforgettable sensory feast. At its heart lies a dish that reigns supreme: Galbi. Perfectly marinated, tender, and bursting with savory-sweet flavors, Galbi Korean BBQ Short Ribs are a true masterpiece. If you dream of recreating that authentic Korean restaurant experience at home, this guide will help you master these iconic short ribs, transforming your dinner into a delicious Korean feast.

## What is Galbi Korean BBQ Short Ribs?
Galbi (갈비), meaning 'rib' in Korean, refers to grilled beef or pork ribs. Most commonly, it's *sogalbi* (beef short ribs). The dish's magic comes from its premium cut and signature marinade. For Galbi Korean BBQ Short Ribs, beef short ribs are usually cut in two ways:
1.  **Flanken-style (LA Galbi):** Thinly cut across the bone, maximizing marinade absorption and allowing quick, even cooking.
2.  **English-style (Deconstructed/Butterfly Cut):** Butterflied or deeply scored along the bone for a larger, tender bite.
The marinade is a symphony of soy sauce, sweetness from fruit (like Asian pear), aromatic garlic and ginger, and sesame oil. This blend tenderizes the meat, infusing it with irresistible umami. Grilled to perfection, the ribs are unbelievably tender, juicy, and caramelized – a true highlight of Korean dinner recipes.
